text:
anita: anyone seeing inference p99 blow up in eastus2 around 09:15? noticed from canary traffic
liam: yep. p99s jumped from ~45ms -> 700-900ms for client-run workloads. Grafana shows host-level packet drops
infra-bot: deploy: host-network-defaults v1.9 rolled out to pool=gpufarm-eastus2 by liam at 09:12 UTC — change: apply host qdisc fq_codel + policing to eth0
sam: that explains it. fq_codel police was intended for egress cost control but wasn't properly scoped to infra lanes
anita: can someone run `sudo tc -s qdisc show dev eth0` on one of affected hosts? sample host gpu-023
maria: paste from gpu-023:
```
qdisc fq_codel 800: root refcnt 2 limit 10240p
 Sent 1.2GiB bytes  packets 145673
 backlog 0b 0p requeues 0
 Policed  packets 4321 bytes 1.6MiB drops 1289 overlimit 1289
```
liam: ugh — 'Policed' >1k drops. that policing is clipping RDMA? RDMA shouldn't be policed but the kernel qdisc was attached to eth0 which RDMA uses in our hosts
sam: RDMA traffic uses mlx5 VF0 but stack still egresses through eth0 for fallback path; misapplied tc ended up policing latency-sensitive kvm->gpu flows
liam: taking canary rollback now — removing qdisc from canary pool and reverting helm host-default-shaper value
anita: command run on gpu-023: `sudo tc qdisc del dev eth0 root` — confirm
maria: removed, retesting. p99 for that host dropped to 50ms within 30s
infra-bot: rollback: host-network-defaults v1.9 rollback applied to pool=gpufarm-canary at 09:18 UTC by liam
sam: we need a followup: update rollout to attach qdisc only to infra-egress interface, add unit-tests to check 'Policed'==0 for rdma and gpu control plane
liam: filed infra-ticket #INFR-4821 with proposed fix and canary gating
anita: :thumbsup: will monitor for 15m then promote rollback if stable
maria: notes: root cause = host-default-shaper helm chart template used interface name variable that defaulted to eth0 in our cloud image change; edge-case for mlx5 hosts
anita: thanks all — nice fast response. still need to check billing impact but SLOs back.
